current_evidence: Not verified: the shared WebFetch budget (400/hour) and the per-turn WebSearch budget were both exhausted before the county's 'making a planning application' page could be fetched, so it is unknown whether this 'Proposed' list was later adopted or replaced.

issues.detail: The workbook link's filename is 'ProposedLocalList...pdf', which points to a consultation-draft local list rather than an adopted one. Grokbot recorded it as 'Captured' with no draft or adopted status. Someone needs to check whether an adopted version exists and what its URL is.

This is a county planning authority, which handles minerals and waste applications and its own Regulation 3 development (for example schools). Even so, 34 of 38 rows are placed under 'Full planning' as 'INFERRED', while 'Minerals & waste (county)' and 'County own devt (Reg 3)' are both '(none)'. Grokbot's own triggers are county-specific: 'mineral and waste management applications, the supporting planning statement should also include', bird-strike measures for mineral restoration, bioaerosols for composting, and 'A Travel Plan is always needed for a new school'. These rows belong under Minerals & waste and Reg 3. The heritage and archaeology statement is also placed under Listed building consent, a type the county does not normally determine, when its trigger is 'developments affecting the historic environment'.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows: 'Minerals & waste (county)': '(none)'; 'County own devt (Reg 3)': '(none)'; 34 rows with notes 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'

issues.detail: Many rows carry text from a different requirement. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' quotes lighting-assessment text (beam angles, light spread), not adverts. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' quotes Agricultural Land Classification and soil-restoration text, which duplicates the ALC row. 'Air Quality Assessment' quotes the Bioaerosol Assessment trigger. 'Coal Mining / Land Stability' quotes the Ventilation/Extraction Statement. 'Design Code / Masterplan' quotes the Landscape Masterplan/Planting Plan. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' quotes the Arboricultural Method Statement/Tree Protection Plan. 'Transport Assessment' quotes the tree/hedgerow survey trigger. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' quotes the LVIA trigger. 'Planning Obligations / S106' quotes the BNG 30-year legal-agreement text. 'Waste / Refuse storage' quotes the minerals and waste planning statement contents.
issues.evidence: e.g. Air Quality row: 'Bioaerosol Assessment Applications that involve the handling, storage or treatment of biodegradable waste, particularly composting applications...'; Coal Mining row: 'Ventilation/Extraction Statement Details of the position and design of any ventilation and extraction equipment...'

issues.detail: Several triggers are fragments or garbled. Health Impact Assessment reads only 'a full HIA may be required.' Block plan reads 'on the Site Plan if the Location Plan scale is not appropriate... vi.' Statement of Community Involvement reads 'of way Statement of Community Involvement Supporting Planning Statement All planning applications which meet the definition set out in the section.' Planning Statement and Waste triggers are dozens of bullet glyphs. Landscaping scheme quotes geodiversity policy references running into the start of a Green Belt Statement. The Drainage/SuDS row quotes foul-drainage text, which duplicates the Foul Sewage row and gives no surface-water or SuDS trigger.

Grokbot's own extracted text names requirements that have no row of their own. Bioaerosol Assessment: applications involving the handling, storage or treatment of biodegradable waste, particularly composting. Lighting Assessment: its content is filed under 'Advertisement drawings'. Green Belt Statement: applications in the Oxford Green Belt. Habitats Regulations / Appropriate Assessment: proposals likely to affect SPAs, SACs or Ramsar sites. Climate Change / Sustainability Statement for all operational development is only partly captured. Since the full PDF was not re-read, other omissions (for example the flood risk assessment trigger) could not be checked.

issues.detail: Most tab_items are not requirements. They include pre-application fee and the 21-working-day response time, file-size limits (10MB/25MB), PDF format, RIBA naming, scan resolution, photograph size, paper-copy rules, a DMPO citation fragment ('...Order 2015 pdf 8 v.'), an Environment Agency guidance link, a table of designated-site types, and 'It would be appreciated if the scale of the plans and paper size is no larger than is required'. In app_type_rows, 'Validation checklist form (completed)' and 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' are both built from pre-application process text, not a validation requirement.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' and 'Policy-driven requirements'; 'Pre-application discussion between the Council, relevant consultees ... will establish what information ... should be submitted'

issues.detail: Rows for Householder, Advertisement consent, Lawful development certificate, Permission in principle and similar types do not apply to a county minerals/waste and Reg 3 authority, which does not determine those applications. They should be marked not applicable rather than 'national requirements only'.

summary: The live source could not be checked because the session's web budgets ran out. Grokbot's link is a 'ProposedLocalList' PDF dated from metadata, so its adopted status and currency are unconfirmed. The extraction treats a county minerals, waste and Reg 3 list as Full planning, leaves the Minerals & waste and Reg 3 types empty, and many rows carry another requirement's trigger text.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The list date of 2025-03-01 comes from PDF metadata (CreationDate), not from an adoption or consultation date in the document text.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The basis label is PDF metadata, as the audit says, but the cover text reads "...COUNTY DEVELOPMENT (REGULATION 3) PLANNING APPLICATIONS March 2025", so 2025-03-01 matches the date printed in the document.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
